sections.h2: How can I sell a house fast in Seattle?
sections.html:
You have three practical routes in Seattle: list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is. Speed depends on the condition of the house, whether tenants live in it, and how much you will spend on repairs first.

Seattle is a big city with a high price tag. The Census Bureau estimates 784,777 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 737,015 in the 2020 census. Only 43.7 percent of Seattle homes are owner-occupied, compared with 65.2 percent nationally.

Here is how the city looks in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures:

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $938,600, against $332,700 for the country as a whole.
  • Median gross rent: $2,030 a month.
  • Median household income: $123,860.
  • Households: 363,466, averaging 2.00 people each.
  • Mean commute to work: 26.0 minutes.

sections.h2: Does Seattle's terrain change how a house sells?
sections.html:
Yes, because hills, water and earthquakes show up on the disclosure form every seller must fill out. Seattle sits between Puget Sound on the west and Lake Washington on the east, and the city is said to lie on seven hills. Capitol Hill, First Hill, Beacon Hill, Queen Anne, Magnolia and West Seattle are the usual list. The highest point inside the city limits is 520 feet above sea level at Myrtle Reservoir Park in High Point.

Seattle is in a major earthquake zone. The magnitude 6.8 Nisqually earthquake on February 28, 2001, caused heavy damage in Pioneer Square, which stands on reclaimed land, and the Seattle Fault runs just south of downtown. The climate is cool and wet in winter, with most of the year's rain falling between October and March, so roofs, basements and drainage get tested every year.

The state seller disclosure form asks about exactly these things. Among its questions are whether the roof has leaked in the last five years, whether the basement has flooded or leaked, whether there has been settling, slippage or sliding of the property, and whether any material damage came from earthquake, floods or landslides. A buyer's inspection will find the same issues you have to disclose.

sections.h2: What do I owe at closing when I sell in Seattle?
sections.html:
The largest line item for most sellers is Washington's real estate excise tax. The seller usually pays it, and if the seller does not, the buyer becomes responsible and an unpaid balance can become a lien on the property. The state portion is graduated, so each slice of the price is taxed at its own rate:

  • 1.1 percent on the part of the price up to $525,000.
  • 1.28 percent on the part from $525,000 to $1,525,000.
  • 2.75 percent on the part from $1,525,000 to $3,025,000.
  • 3 percent on anything above $3,025,000.

The Department of Revenue shows new break points for sales beginning January 1, 2027: $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000, with the same four rates. As an illustration only, a sale at the $938,600 Census median value that closes before that date would carry roughly $11,069 of state tax ($5,775 on the first $525,000 plus $5,294 on the remaining $413,600). A local rate is added on top, and the Department of Revenue publishes a local rate table. Ask the King County treasurer or your closing agent which local rate applies to a Seattle address.

The tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, which the state treats as the date the deed is notarized. If it is not paid within one month, interest runs on the unpaid amount, and the Department of Revenue lists a 6 percent rate for 2026 and 2027. Keep sale records for at least four years, since the state can audit a sale. Ask the King County treasurer for your parcel's property tax balance and due dates.

sections.h2: What paperwork does a Seattle seller have to hand over?
sections.html:
For an improved residential property, the seller must deliver a completed disclosure statement to the buyer unless the buyer has waived it or the transfer is exempt. Under RCW 64.06.020, delivery is due within five business days after both sides accept a written purchase contract, unless they agree otherwise.

The buyer then has three business days from delivery to rescind in writing, and the buyer may waive that right. The form is signed by the seller alone and is not a warranty. It covers title, water, sewer, structure, systems, homeowners' associations and environmental conditions, and it reminds the seller that carbon monoxide alarms and a smoke detection device must be in place.

Questions about work done on the house deserve extra care. The form asks whether there were conversions, additions or remodeling, and if so, whether all building permits and final inspections were obtained. If you finished a basement or added a bedroom years ago, pull your records before you answer.

sections.h2: I own a Seattle rental. What rules apply before I sell?
sections.html:
If tenants live in the house, two sets of rules apply: the city's rental registration program and the state's rules for ending a tenancy. Under the Rental Registration and Inspection Ordinance, rental housing must be registered with the city as soon as there is a tenant, and short-term rentals that are not the operator's primary residence must register before they are listed. A registration lasts two years. Fees and costs from the Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections are below.

ItemAmount
Registration, one rental unit$126
Each additional unit at the same property$31.50
City inspector, one rental unit$241.50
City inspector, each additional unit$52.50
Filing fee for a private inspector's results$63
Penalty for a violation$150 a day for the first 10 days, then $500 a day

Source: Seattle SDCI, RRIO owners and managers. Properties are selected for an inspection once in the first five years, with a 10 percent chance of a second selection in the next five. A notice gives at least 60 days to finish the inspection, and tenants must get at least two days' notice of the visit. Missing smoke or carbon monoxide detectors, missing handrails and exposed wiring are among the common failures. The RRIO helpline is (206) 684-4110.

For a single-family house, RCW 59.18.650 lets an owner end a tenancy to sell with at least 90 days' advance written notice. The statute treats the owner as electing to sell only if the house is listed at a reasonable price within 30 days after the tenant leaves, and it presumes no intent to sell if the owner relists it as a rental or pulls it from the market within 90 days. A landlord who removes a tenant in violation of the section owes the greater of the tenant's damages or three times the monthly rent, plus attorney fees and court costs.

sections.h2: Which roads, schools and transit lines shape demand in Seattle?
sections.html:
Seattle Public Schools serves the vast majority of the city, and a small part of the Delridge neighborhood falls inside the Highline School District. Only Madison Street runs east to west without a break, and only Interstate 5 and State Route 99 run uninterrupted from north to south.

Rail has changed which addresses are convenient. Link light rail's 1 Line reached Northgate in October 2021 and Lynnwood in August 2024, and the 2 Line opened between Bellevue and Redmond in April 2024 and was extended to Seattle in March 2026. Regional voters approved Sound Transit 3 in November 2016, which calls for light rail to West Seattle and Ballard. The Alaskan Way Viaduct was replaced by a tunnel in 2019.

Amazon, Starbucks, Expeditors International of Washington, Nordstrom, Weyerhaeuser, Expedia Group and Zillow had their headquarters in Seattle on the Fortune 500's 2022 list, and the Port of Seattle is a major trade gateway.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for a Seattle house?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits a house that needs repairs, an inherited property, a rental with difficult tenants, or a seller who must move on a fixed date. Before you accept any offer, check these items:

  • Ask who pays the state and local excise tax and any title or escrow charges, and get the answer in writing.
  • Confirm the closing date and whether the buyer will accept the house with tenants in place.
  • Compare the offer with recent sales of similar homes near you.
  • Check your rental registration status with the RRIO program if the house has been rented.
  • Collect permits for any additions, since you still answer the permit question on the seller disclosure form.

You can request a cash offer for your Seattle house and compare it with a listing estimate before you decide. The excise tax and property tax items above apply either way.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax when I sell a house in Seattle?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays it. If the seller does not, the buyer is responsible, and an unpaid amount can create a lien on the property. The tax goes to the county treasurer on the date of sale, and the state rate is graduated from 1.1 percent up to 3 percent, with a local rate added.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a disclosure statement in Seattle?
faqs.a: Yes, in most sales of improved residential property. RCW 64.06.020 requires delivery within five business days after the contract is accepted, unless the buyer waived the statement or the transfer is exempt. The buyer then has three business days to rescind in writing.

faqs.q: Do I need to register my Seattle rental before I sell it?
faqs.a: If it has a tenant, it should be registered. Seattle requires registration as soon as there is a tenant in the rental space, and a registration lasts two years. Late registration or a missed inspection can bring penalties of $150 a day for the first 10 days and $500 a day after that.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Seattle house that has tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer can purchase it with the lease in place. If you want the tenant out so you can sell a single-family house, RCW 59.18.650 requires at least 90 days' written notice and a genuine attempt to list the house within 30 days after the tenant leaves.

faqs.q: What if my Seattle house has an addition built without a permit?
faqs.a: You can still sell it, but you must answer the permit question on the state disclosure form honestly. The form asks whether additions or remodeling were done and whether permits and final inspections were obtained. Ask the Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections what records exist for your address.
